chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard him say: “If you do not find water and you intend tayammum, then delay tayammum until the end of the time. For if water escapes you, the earth will not escape you.”

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end portion of the prescribed prayer time
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl when water is unavailable
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the earth or earth-material used for tayammum

ai.seo_question: When should tayammum be performed if water is not available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about tayammum when water is unavailable. It instructs delaying tayammum until the end of the prayer time, since water may become available, while the earth—used for tayammum—remains accessible as a means of purification.
